o.text: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *ses. Cognate with Turkmen, Crimean Tatar, Gagauz, Turkish ses, Kazakh сес (ses), Chuvash сасӑ (sas̬ă).
Borrowed from Arabic أَسَاسًا (ʔasāsan), adverbial accusative of أَسَاس (ʔasās). By surface analysis, əsas + -ən.
Borrowed from Classical Persian اهل قلم (ahl-i qalam).

From Proto-Turkic *sok- (“to pierce, stick into”), which was homonyms to and possibly cognate with Proto-Turkic *sok- (“to hit, beat, crush”). Compare Karakhanid سُقْماق (suqmāq), Turkish sokmak (“to insert”), etc.
Borrowed from Classical Persian قَحْبِهخانِه (qahba-xāna). By surface analysis, qəhbə + -xana.
